messages:
mira: quick note — ran int4 conversion of Llama4->Gemma-lite with head-sparsity pruning and saw a consistent drop on our summarization evals. :eyes:

mira: perf numbers: fp16 baseline rouge-L=0.72, int4 w/ per-head quant=0.69, int4 + sparse-headmap=0.65 (surprising).

sam: ugh. can you paste the exact conversion flags?

mira: yup: `convert.py --src llama4 --tgt gemma-lite --quant int4 --per_head --sparsity 0.25 --proj-order keep`

mira: also noticed odd logits when running long-context tests — repeating tokens around token id boundaries (token ids near 32000).

kai: repeating near high token ids screams tokenizer/vocab aliasing to me. did you remap the sentinels?

mira: we used the naive tokenmap from the exporter. didn’t run anything fancy.

sam: could be rotary-phase nonuniformity across pruned heads. If you prune heads asymmetrically the summed rotary angles per position can shift.

mira: that aligns with a quick KV-sanity check — attention weight norms drop for a subset of heads after conversion.

bench-bot: automated run finished — longctx-smoke: baseline_perp=12.4, converted_perp=12.9, sparse_headmap_perp=13.7. See /bench/results/5123456799/*.log

kai: interesting. two hypotheses: (1) token id aliasing causing stray positional wrap; (2) per-head scale/phase not preserved when we collapse projection order during conversion.

sam: agree. quick repro: run the same prompt but with a single-step attention trace. dump rotary cos/sin for head 3/7/11 pre/post conversion.

mira: doing that now. quick snippet I’m running:```python
# trace rotary for head 7
att = model.layers[10].attn
state = att.kv_cache.get(slice(0,64))
cos, sin = att.rotary.cache[:64, head=7]
print(cos[:6])
```

mira: early output shows phase vectors are shifted by ~0.003-0.01 for pruned config (per-element).

sam: that's enough to change token alignment downstream over long contexts. Small phase offsets accumulate.

kai: mitigation plan: (A) rebuild tokenmap with wrap-aware remapping for high ids, (B) enforce headwise phase rescaling during conversion (match per-head mean), (C) run int4 reconf with symmetric head pruning.

mira: I’ll try B first — rescale phases so mean(cos, sin) per-head matches baseline.

sam: add a control: run on a short eval set (100 examples) to see immediate delta before doing full bench.

mira: short-run results: rescale(B) recovered rouge-L to 0.71 (int4+sparse -> 0.71). repeating tokens reduced.

kai: sounds promising. still do A in parallel, token aliasing might bite other models.

sam: add an extra unit test to conversion: compare cumulative rotary phase per-head across models and assert < 1e-3 difference. If failing, conversion should fail-fast.

mira: noted. filing a tiny PR for conversion tool and adding bench case. will ping for review.

bench-bot: queued full-bench (n=2k) — will post results in thread when done. :rotating_light:

mira: thanks — will follow up with logs and a patch.
